utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-A, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me begin by making sure that the audio equipment is working properly. Let me ask the appellants whether they hear the proceedings in a language they understand, beginning with Mr. Prlic. THE APPELLANT PRLIC: Yes, I understand well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojic. THE APPELLANT STOJIC: [Interpretation] Yes, everything is all right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Praljak. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petkovic. THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] It's all right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Coric. THE APPELLANT CORIC: [Interpretation] Everything is fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Pusic. THE APPELLANT PUSIC: Everything is fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARSDEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. For the Prosecution, Katharine Marsden, Laurel Baig, and our case manager, Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we've already had the appearances of the Prosecution, and now I will turn to the Defence. For Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Suzana Tomanovic, co-counsel for Dr. Jadranko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Tomanovic. For Mr. Stojic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Mr. Stojic is represented by Ms. Senka Nozica, lead counsel. I am co-counsel in the case. My name is Karim Khan of Queen's Counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: For Mr. Petkovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Vesna Alaburic, counsel for Mr. Milivoj Petkovic. And this young girl is Bettina Spilker, our legal counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC-TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I don't know if it is politically correct to call somebody young girl, you are all young.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But she is really very young.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: For Mr. Coric, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC-TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Defence of Mr. Coric, Ms. Dijana Tomasegovic-Tomic, lead counsel; and Drazen Plavec, co-counsel; as well as Stephane Bourgon as legal advisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAHOTA
utterances.text: Mr. President, on behalf of Berislav Pusic, I represent him today as co-counsel. My name is Raj Sahota, and I am assisted by my learned colleague, Mr. Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, all. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes: First, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their detention conditions, and for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. Second, it provides an opportunity to the update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on 8 October 2013. Today's Status Conference is scheduled by an order filed on 16 January 2014. Let me begin the Status Conference by inquiring into the status of the detention conditions and health situation of the appellants. If any of the appellants wishes, this discussion could take place in closed sessions. So let me start for Mr. Prlic. Mr. Prlic, do you have any matters to raise? Mr. Stojic, would you like to respond or Mr. Prlic himself? Mr. Prlic. THE APPELLANT PRLIC: No, I don't have any matter to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Praljak. My question was to Mr. Praljak. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So now we will move to Mr. Petkovic. THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] I have nothing to raise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Coric. THE APPELLANT CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, nothing to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Pusic. THE APPELLANT PUSIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no issues. Whatever there is to say will be said be my Defence counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question to Mr. Stojic. We don't want to discriminate against you, I can assure you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. It's all right. I have no issues. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and I'm glad that none of you has problems in terms of your detention or health that you would like to raise with me. Recent procedural update of the case. The update, I recall that the notices of appeal of Mr. Praljak and Mr. Pusic were filed on 20 June 2013 and that the notice of the appeal of the Prosecution was filed on 27 August 2013. On 21 June 2013, upon a request of the parties, I ordered that the notices of appeal of Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Petkovic, and Mr. Coric be filed within 60 days of the issuance of the official English translation of the trial judgement. I further recall that I ordered Mr. Praljak, Mr. Pusic, and the Prosecution to file their appeal briefs no later than 135 days from the issuance of the official English translation of the trial judgement and that as a result there is a harmonised briefing schedule in place for all parties. I note that the decision on the filings pertaining to the motions filed by the Prosecution and Mr. Pusic concerning the latter's Notice of Appeal, filed on 15 and on 26 July 2013, respectively, will be delivered in due course. On 3 October 2013, Mr. Praljak filed a public motion requesting a stay of proceedings until he receives the translation of various documents into a language he understands, which is B/C/S. On 4 October 2013, Mr. Praljak filed a public motion requesting the assignment of his formerly Tribunal-paid counsel under the Tribunal's legal aid provisions that apply to level 3 cases. I note that the Appeals Chamber has received all filings pertaining to these matters and will deal with Mr. Praljak's requests of 3 and 4 October in due course. On 20 January 2014, the Registrar filed a public application for the recovering of legal aid and funds from Mr. Praljak. On 27 January 2014, Mr. Praljak filed his response requesting the Appeals Chamber to deny the application and to order the Registrar to provide him with the details, specification of the costs spent on his Defence. Issues raised by the parties. At this point I would like to ask the parties whether they have any issues that they would like to raise at this time. Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me start from the Prosecution. Are there any issues the Prosecution would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARSDEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. And of the appellants, let me ask that in order. Mr. Prlic. I will come to you, Mr. Praljak. Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question to ask, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Sorry, I could not hear you. Could you kindly repeat? I had a problem. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask just one question. After the judgement, the Registrar informed us that the English translation of the judgement would be finished by June 2014 at the latest. I would like to know if there is an update with this regard, and if not, if it would be possible for the Registrar to inform us at least 30 days in advance of the completion of the translation so that we may be able to organise our work back home since a dead-line of two months for an announcement of the -- of a notice of appeal is not a long time. Especially bearing in mind the bulk of the judgement, about four and a half thousand pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Actually, as of this morning the expectation was that the English translation would in fact become available in June 2014. As it is, I've instructed my staff this morning to check with the Registrar that there are no changes. This is information which I have received as late as December, so I do hope that it's still valid. If not, I see your point about being informed prior to the completion of the translation so you can prepare. It's a very reasonable one and we will try to respect it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I only have one request. If possible, since our defendant does not speak English, it would be extremely useful for him, as he wants to take part in the appeal proceedings, for a -- it will be good for him for a Croatian translation of the judgement to be available as soon as possible. We would kindly ask you to exert influence to the effect that a Croatian translation become possible -- become available as soon as possible, if not at the same time as the English translation, so that it may be used during the appeals proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I will do everything I can to make sure that the Croatian translation would be available if not at the same time as the English one, very soon thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: We will work on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. Now we will move on to Mr. Praljak. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Meron, I did not request a specification of costs. It was the Tribunal that requested that from the Registrar to know what the Registrar thinks, I owe him. I never requested anything like that because I refuse any idea that I lied and concealed anything. I have no money to pay for the proceedings. In the letter I sent to you and in previous documents, I only requested the proceedings against me to be just; in other words, that the other side also be heard and that its arguments be taken into account. Unfortunately, the Registrar did not do that. Their reason was that there was no money and unfortunately the judgement was passed without me in any -- or, rather, the decision was taken without me in any way being able to influence it. I kindly ask that you, or the Appeals Chamber too, hear the other side too, to take into consideration my arguments. I state that a huge campaign was waged against me by the Registrar, a campaign that abounded in untruthful allegations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: We expect that a reply from the Registrar to a response [Microphone not activated] week or so -- sorry. I apologise. We are awaiting a reply from the Registrar to the response which you submitted on 27 January, and we hope that it will come before long and then we will be able to decide on this matter. We hope that maybe next week we'll be getting something from the Registrar. So I can assure you that we are not neglecting it. We are working on it. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, Mr. Meron. I hope in all honesty that the documents in my response to the Prosecution, which amounts to 103 pages, will at least be gone through so that someone has a look at it. No matter what your decision may be, I will accept it. But that the decision would be made without ever gaining insight into my documentation, well, I apologise, but I think I've already communicated my position in a letter sent to you previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I can assure you that we go very carefully through documentation submitted. THE APPELLANT PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Next is Mr. Petkovic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Two already raised the issues by my colleagues of something relevant for Petkovic Defence as well. Thank you for the answers, no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC-TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no other issues to raise in addition to those raised by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And finally, Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAHOTA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we very briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Registrar, private session, please.
